Why is this? Because the great ocean is an immeasurable vessel.
O Sons of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: dwelling on the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), they are able to receive the great rain of the light of the Dharma from one Buddha; and from two, three, four, five, ten, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, a hundred million, up to an immeasurable, boundless, ineffable, limitless number that transcends all calculation—within a single thought-moment, they are able to fully endure and receive such great clouds of Dharma from all these Buddhas.
"For this reason, this stage is named the Stage of the Dharma-Cloud. He asked:
"O Son of the Buddha!"
"How much of the great rain of the light of the Buddha-dharma can this bodhisattva endure and receive within a single thought-moment?
He replied, "It cannot be known by calculation; it can only be described through analogy."
O Sons of the Buddha!

Suppose there were as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of worlds throughout the ten directions; and suppose all the sentient beings in those atom-like worlds were to attain the *dhāraṇī* of hearing and retaining, become attendants of Buddhas, and become great *śrāvakas* foremost in erudition—just as, for example, the bhikṣu Mahāvicaya was foremost in erudition under the Tathāgata Vajrapadma.
One sentient being achieves such power of extensive learning, and the same is true for as many other sentient beings.
The Dharma received by one person is not received again by a second; in this manner, all are distinct from one another.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
What do you think?
Is the power of the extensive learning maintained by all these sentient beings great?"
He replied, "Immeasurable. "O Sons of the Buddha!"

I shall now explain this for you: when a bodhisattva dwells in this stage of the Cloud of Dharma, in a single thought-moment and at a single instant, within the presence of a single Buddha, they are able to receive and sustain the treasury of the dharma-nature of the three periods of time, which is called the "Rain of the Great Dharma-Light. Compared to this, the power of the extensive learning of all sentient beings above—even taken as a whole—does not equal one hundredth part; it does not equal one thousandth, ten-thousandth, one hundred-thousandth, ten-millionth, nor even one *nayuta*th part; indeed, it cannot be reached by any calculation or analogy.

Just as one can hear from a single Buddha, so too all the Buddhas—as numerous as the atoms within the various worlds of the ten directions—are able to receive the great rain of the light of Dharma; furthermore, they are able to exceed this limit, receiving the great rain of the light of Dharma in its entirety, immeasurable and boundless, all at once and in a single thought-moment. For this reason, it is called the Ground of the Cloud of Dharma (Dharmameghā-bhūmi).
"Furthermore, Sons of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas dwell in this Great Dharma Cloud Stage (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), by the power of their own vows, they give rise to great compassion and emit the thunderous sound of the Great Dharma; they take the various supernormal powers, clarities, and fearlessnesses as lightning flashes; they produce great wisdom as a swift wind; they take great merit and roots of goodness as dense clouds; they manifest various bodily forms and colors as multicolored clouds; and they preach the Dharma and subdue Māras as the rumbling of thunder. In a single thought-moment and at one time, they are able to pervade all the aforementioned worlds as numerous as atoms, without exception, and even beyond that number."

Because it rains the Dharma of goodness and the nectar-like rain of the Dharma, it extinguishes the dust and flames of affliction that arise from ignorance and according to the inclinations of sentient beings; therefore, it is called the Ground of the Dharma-Cloud (*dharmameghā bhūmi*).
"Furthermore, O Sons of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas abide in this Dharma-Cloud Stage (Dharmameghā-bhūmi), within a single world-system they descend from the Tuṣita Heaven and perform all Buddha-deeds up to the manifestation of Great Parinirvāṇa; for the sake of those beings to be converted, they manifest spiritual powers accordingly.

Whether it be in two or three thousand-world systems, or even in worlds as numerous as the atoms mentioned above, or further in hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of asaṃkhyeya worlds, they descend from Tuṣita and perform all Buddha-deeds up to the manifestation of Great Parinirvāṇa; for the sake of those beings to be converted, they manifest spiritual powers accordingly."

"When this bodhisattva dwells in this stage, they attain supreme mastery over wisdom and the power of excellent discernment; they may make a narrow land wide or a wide land narrow, or make a defiled land pure."
In this way, all the natures of the world possess spiritual power.

This bodhisattva may, within a single minute particle (*paramāṇu*), display a trichiliocosm with its Iron Ring Mountains and rivers and valleys without any crowding; or he may cause the various adornments of two, three, four, five, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, or even a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, a million, ten million, a billion, an immeasurable, or an unspeakably unspeakable number of worlds to all enter into a single minute particle.

Whether they manifest the adornments of a single world within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds; or whether they place even the sentient beings of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds into a single world without it becoming cramped; or whether they place the sentient beings of a single world into unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds; or whether they manifest unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds adhering to the tip of a single hair without distressing the sentient beings; or whether they manifest within a single hair all the adorned displays of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas.
Or, with as many atoms as there are in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds throughout the ten directions, they manifest such bodies within a single thought-moment;
within each body, they display countless hands, using these hands to diligently and wholeheartedly make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions;

with each hand, they grasp clusters of lotuses as numerous as the sands of the Ganges to scatter over the Buddhas, and likewise with ointments, blended incenses, powdered incenses, robes, banners, canopies, and precious objects—all such articles of adornment are held in their hands to make offerings to the Buddhas.
It was likewise for each and every body.

Furthermore, from each and every body, there were emanated as many heads as there are atoms in those lands, and upon each head were as many tongues as there are atoms in those lands, whereby they praised all Buddhas through such supernormal power.

Such matters as these fill the ten directions in every thought-moment; in every thought-moment, by means of supernormal powers, they manifest the attainment of the Buddha-way, the turning of the wheel of Dharma, and even the Great Parinirvāṇa within immeasurable worlds.

“Within the three periods of time, they manifest immeasurable bodies through their supernormal powers; within their own bodies, they manifest the adornments of the immeasurable and boundless buddha-fields of the Buddhas; within their own bodies, they demonstrate the formation and destruction of all worlds; or they cause all winds to emerge from a single pore without afflicting sentient beings.”

Or, one might wish to make immeasurable and boundless worlds into a single sea of water; within this sea-water, one creates a great lotus flower whose form, color, and radiance illuminate immeasurable and boundless worlds, therein manifesting the wondrous events of attaining the adornments of Bodhi, up to and including the manifestation of the attainment of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

All the radiance of the mani-jewels, lightning, the sun, the moon, and the stars within one's own body, as well as all luminous objects throughout the worlds of the ten directions, all appear within that body.
By blowing air from his mouth, he can cause all the infinite and boundless worlds of the ten directions to tremble, yet without causing sentient beings to have any thought of alarm or fear.
He manifests the exhaustion of the water kalpa, the wind kalpa, and the fire kalpa in the worlds of the ten directions, yet the bodies of sentient beings remain adorned according to their wishes.

Or they may wish to manifest their own body as the body of a Tathāgata, transform the body of a Tathāgata into their own body, transform the body of a Tathāgata into their own Buddha-land, or transform their own Buddha-land into the body of a Tathāgata.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Such are the miraculous transformations of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva on this Bodhisattva Stage of the Cloud of Dharma (dharmameghā).
Furthermore, there are other immeasurable, sovereign, and wondrous displays of supernormal powers."

At that time, there were in the assembly various bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra-devendra, Brahmā-rāja, the Caturmahārājas, Īśvara-devaputra, the Śuddhāvāsa devas, and others, each of whom thought to themselves:
"If the power of the supernatural faculties and the power of wisdom of a bodhisattva are thus immeasurable and boundless, what then must the Buddha be like?"
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vimukticandra, knowing what was in the minds of the great assembly, asked the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha:
"O Son of the Buddha!
Now this great assembly all harbors doubts; having heard of the power of this bodhisattva’s great supernormal faculties and wisdom, they have fallen into a web of uncertainty.
You should now sever all their doubts and demonstrate the wondrous deeds of a bodhisattva’s supernormal adornments.
Immediately, the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha entered the samādhi of the Essential Nature of All Buddha-lands.

At that time, the great assembly—consisting of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra-devendra, Brahmā-devaputra, the World-protecting Kings (Lokapālas), Īśvara-devaputra, the Śuddhāvāsa devas, and others—all perceived themselves entering into the body of the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha. Within his body, they beheld the various adornments of a trichiliocosm, such that even if one were to describe them for an entire kalpa, they could not be exhausted.

Within that [space], he saw the tree of the Buddha’s place of enlightenment; its trunk was ten thousand three-thousandfold world systems in circumference, it rose a million three-thousandfold world systems in height, and its canopy spread over three hundred billion three-thousandfold world systems.
The height and breadth of the tree were immeasurable, and there was a lion throne upon it; on that throne sat a Buddha named Sarvajñatā-rāja Tathāgata.

The entire great assembly beheld the Buddha seated upon the throne, and as for all the magnificent and sublime articles of offering that adorned it, even if one were to describe them for an entire kalpa, they could not be exhausted.
After the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha had manifested such great supernormal powers, he returned the great assembly to their respective places.
At that time, the entire assembly conceived a sense of wonder and, with silent, single-minded attention, gazed upon the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra addressed the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha!
It is truly rare; this samādhi possesses great power."
"What is the name of this samādhi? He replied,
"This samādhi is named the Essential Nature of All Buddha-lands."
He asked: "To what extent does the power of this samādhi reach? He replied:
“O Son of the Buddha!

If a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has skillfully cultivated and perfected this power of samādhi, they can manifest within their own body as many trichiliocosm worlds as there are atoms in immeasurable Ganges-sands of worlds, and even more than that number.”
“O Son of the Buddha!
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva abides in this Dharma-Cloud Stage (Dharmameghā-bhūmi), they attain such immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Bodhisattva samādhis.”

For this reason, when this bodhisattva dwells in this stage, his physical actions are difficult to fathom; his verbal actions are difficult to fathom; his mental actions are difficult to fathom; his sovereign spiritual powers are difficult to fathom; his contemplation of the dharmas of the three periods of time is difficult to fathom; his entry into the practices of various samādhis is difficult to fathom; his power of wisdom is difficult to fathom; his playful mastery of the various liberations is difficult to fathom; and what he performs through transformations, through spiritual powers, and through his inherent force is difficult to fathom. Briefly stated, even such things as his lifting and lowering of his feet cannot be fathomed by even minor princes or bodhisattvas who dwell in the Stage of Sublime Virtue (*sādhumatī*).
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Such is the immeasurability of the Bodhisattva’s Stage of the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā bhūmi*); it has now been briefly explained.
Were it to be explained in detail, it could not be exhausted even in the course of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) eons."
He asked: "O Son of the Buddha!

If such are the power of the sphere of activity and the power of the supernormal knowledges of a bodhisattva, then what are the power of the sphere of activity and the power of the supernormal knowledges of a Buddha?"
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!
It is, for example, as if someone were to take two or three clods of earth from among the four continents and say:”
"Is the nature of the ground of infinite worlds more numerous than this?
Regarding what you have asked, I say it is so.
How can one seek to measure the immeasurable wisdom of a Tathāgata with the wisdom of a bodhisattva?
O Sons of the Buddha!
It is as if a person were to take a small portion of the earth-element from among the four continents, while the remainder remains exceedingly vast.
Even for the Bodhisattva’s Dharma-Cloud Stage (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), one could only speak of it over the course of immeasurable eons; how much more so for the stage of the Tathāgata?
"O Sons of the Buddha!
I now proclaim this so that you may know it, with the Buddhas of the present as my witnesses.

Suppose there were as many Buddha-worlds as there are atoms in the infinite and boundless worlds of each and every direction, and these worlds were entirely filled with Bodhisattvas of the tenth stage—like a dense forest of rice or hemp. Although these Bodhisattvas possess infinite and boundless karma, having cultivated the merits, wisdom, and meditative concentrations of a Bodhisattva, they do not equal even one hundredth part of the power of the Tathāgata’s merit and wisdom; they do not equal even one part in a hundred-thousand-million-billionth part, nor can they be reached by any calculation or analogy."
"O Sons of the Buddha!

These Bodhisattvas, following such wisdom, accord with the body, speech, and mind of the Tathāgatas; yet they do not abandon the samādhis of the Bodhisattvas, but diligently make offerings to the Buddhas. Throughout each and every kalpa, they offer all manner of coarse and subtle requisites to immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, and are able to fully receive the spiritual powers of those Buddhas, which become increasingly bright and superior."

Regarding this Bodhisattva’s inquiry and debate concerning the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), there is no one who can surpass them; even throughout immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons, they could never be exhausted.
"O Son of the Buddha!..."

It is like a master goldsmith who skillfully refines this gold into an ornamental object, interspersing it with unsurpassed mani-jewels and placing it upon the neck of the Sovereign Heavenly King (Īśvara), such that none of the other devas are able to seize it.
Furthermore, no ornaments of the devas and humans can equal them.
O Sons of the Buddha!
When Bodhisattvas dwell within the ten stages, their wisdom, merit, and roots of goodness cannot be equaled by any Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas from the first stage through the ninth stage.
"Because a bodhisattva dwelling in this stage attains the illumination of great wisdom, they are able to accord with all wisdom; the light of any other wisdom cannot destroy it."
For example, O Son of the Buddha!

The radiance of the Great Lord Maheśvara King reaches all places of birth, such that the light of other sentient beings cannot equal it; it is able to bring coolness and relief to the bodies and minds of sentient beings.
O Sons of the Buddha!

It is the same for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas: dwelling in this Dharma-Cloud Stage (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), their wisdom and radiance cannot be equaled by any Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, nor can they be equaled by Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas from the first stage up to the ninth stage.
When these bodhisattvas dwell in this stage, they are able to cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the path to all-knowledge.
"O Sons of the Buddha!

When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas dwell in this stage, the Buddhas of the ten directions expound wisdom for them so that they may penetrate the three periods of time, correctly know the characteristics of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), universally cover all worlds with wisdom, illuminate the nature of all worlds, universally cover all sentient beings with great compassion and great kindness, and correctly and universally perceive and know all dharmas."
To state the essentials: he fully explains the path leading to all-knowledge.
"O Son of the Buddha!
This is called the tenth Bodhisattva stage of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, the Cloud of Dharma."

"When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this stage, he frequently becomes the Heavenly King Maheśvara. His wisdom is clear and penetrating; he skillfully expounds the *pāramitās* of the Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Bodhisattvas. Regarding the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), no one who raises questions or objections is able to exhaust his discourse."

Whatever wholesome deeds they perform—whether through giving, kind speech, beneficial action, or cooperation—all are never apart from mindfulness of the Buddha, mindfulness of the Dharma, mindfulness of the bodhisattva companions, mindfulness of the bodhisattva practices, mindfulness of the various pāramitās, and mindfulness of the practices of the stages; they are never apart from mindfulness of the ten powers, mindfulness of the fearlessnesses, and mindfulness of the unique qualities, up to and including mindfulness of the perfection of all-knowledge.
He constantly reflects:

"When shall I become the foremost among sentient beings, the most excellent, the greatest, the most sublime, the highest, the unsurpassed, the guide, the leader, the teacher, and the venerable one—even becoming the ultimate refuge for all sentient beings?"

If one wishes to practice such diligent vigor, in a single thought-moment one attains as many samādhis as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of worlds, and even manifests as many bodhisattva retinues as those atoms. If, through the power of vows, one’s spiritual transformations are sovereign, they further exceed these numbers—namely, the supreme and wondrous offerings of all practices, the arising of karma through faith and understanding, whether by body, speech, radiance, faculties, supernormal powers, voice, or sphere of activity, for as many as hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas beyond measure.
“O Sons of the Buddha!
This is called the sequential progression through the stages of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, proceeding toward all-encompassing wisdom (sarvākārajñatā).
O Sons of the Buddha!”
For example, just as the four rivers flow forth from Lake Anavatapta, filling the four continents, increasing further and further without exhaustion until they enter the great ocean;
so it is, O Sons of the Buddha!

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: from the Bodhisattva flow the waters of the great vows of roots of goodness; by means of the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), they satisfy sentient beings without exhaustion, increasing further and further until reaching all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).
“O Sons of the Buddha!
These ten stages of the bodhisattvas exist with their distinctions because of the Buddha’s wisdom.
It is like how, because of the great earth, there are ten great mountain kings.”
What are these ten? They are:

the King of Mountains Himavat, the King of Mountains Gandhamādana, the King of Mountains Kailāsa, the King of Mountains Ṛṣigiri, the King of Mountains Yugandhara, the King of Mountains Aśvakarṇa, the King of Mountains Nimindhara, the King of Mountains Cakravāḍa, the King of Mountains Viśvaka, and the King of Mountains Sumeru.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as all medicinal herbs are gathered within the King of Snowy Mountains and cannot be exhausted by taking them, so it is,
O Sons of the Buddha!"
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva is also like this: dwelling in the Bodhisattva Stage of Joy, all the world’s scriptures, arts, literary verses, and incantations are contained therein, without end.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as all varieties of incense are gathered within the King of Fragrant Mountains (Gandhamādana) and can never be exhausted;

so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who dwells in the Bodhisattva Ground of Freedom from Defilement (vimalā-bhūmi): the observance of precepts, the dhūta practices, majestic deportment, and the accumulation of factors conducive to enlightenment are gathered therein, without end."
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as Mount Kailāsa, the king of mountains, is composed solely of jewels and gathers all manner of exquisite flowers that can never be exhausted;
so it is, O Sons of the Buddha!"

The Bodhisattva is likewise; abiding in the Stage of Radiance (*prabhākari-bhūmi*), they gather all worldly meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), and gateways of samādhi, which are inexhaustible.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as the King of Mountains, the Mountain of Sages and Saints, is composed solely of jewels and contains an inexhaustible multitude of sages possessing the five supernormal powers;
so it is, O Sons of the Buddha!"

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: dwelling in the Bodhisattva stage of Radiance (Arciṣmatī), they gather the causes and conditions for sentient beings to enter the Path, such that various questions and challenges can never be exhausted.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as Mount Yugandhara, the king of mountains, is composed solely of jewels and gathers an inexhaustible multitude of great yakṣas and yakṣa-rākṣasas; so too is it with this assembly."
O Sons of the Buddha!

It is the same for the Bodhisattva: dwelling in the Bodhisattva stage of Difficult to Conquer, they gather all forms of mastery and supernormal powers (*ṛddhi-vidhi*), which are inexhaustible to describe.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as the King of Mountains, Aśvakarṇa, is composed solely of jewels and gathers all manner of exquisite fruits that can never be exhausted;
so it is, O Sons of the Buddha!"

In the same way, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in the stage of Presence (Abhimukhī), they gather the profound principle of dependent origination and explain the fruits of the śrāvakas, which can never be exhausted.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as Mount Nimiṃdhara, the king of mountains, is composed solely of jewels and gathers all the powerful nāgas and devas in inexhaustible numbers."
O Sons of the Buddha!

It is the same for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva: dwelling in the Bodhisattva stage of Far-Going (Dūraṃgamā), they gather various skillful means and wisdoms to expound the path of the Pratyekabuddha, which is inexhaustible.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as Mount Khadiraka, the king of mountains, is composed solely of jewels, so too the collection of the minds of those who have attained mastery cannot be exhausted.
O Sons of the Buddha!"

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: dwelling in the Immovable Stage (*acalā-bhūmi*), they gather all the paths of mastery of the Bodhisattvas and discourse upon the nature of the world, which is inexhaustible.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as the King of Mountains, Sumeru, is composed entirely of jewels and is the gathering place for great spiritual powers and all the asuras without end;
so it is, O Sons of the Buddha!"

The Bodhisattva is also like this: dwelling in the wondrous and virtuous stage of a Bodhisattva, they gather and transform the practices of sentient beings through wisdom, explaining the characteristics of the world in a manner that can never be exhausted.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
Just as Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains, is composed solely of jewels and gathers all the celestial deities without end;
so it is, O Sons of the Buddha!"
The Bodhisattva is likewise; dwelling in the stage of the Cloud of Dharma, they gather the ten powers and four fearlessnesses of the Tathāgata to proclaim all Buddha-dharmas, which are inexhaustible.
“O Sons of the Buddha!
These ten jewel mountains all exist within the great ocean, yet they possess distinct characteristics because of the waters of the great ocean;
likewise, the ten stages of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas also exist within the Buddha’s wisdom, yet they possess distinct characteristics because of the omniscience [of that wisdom].”
“O Sons of the Buddha!
For example, the great ocean is reckoned as the ‘great ocean’ by virtue of ten characteristics, and none can destroy it. What are these ten?

1. It is gradually deep; 2. it does not dwell together with corpses; 3. other waters lose their original names upon entering it; 4. it has a single taste; 5. it is a vast accumulation of treasures; 6. it is extremely deep and difficult to enter; 7. it is vast and immeasurable; 8. it is the dwelling place for many beings of great body; 9. it does not exceed its constant limits; 10. it can receive all great rains without overflowing.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
The practices of all Bodhisattvas are likewise; by virtue of ten causes and conditions, they are named 'incapable of being destroyed. What are these ten?
In the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), one gradually generates firm vows;
in the Stage Free from Defilement (*vimalā-bhūmi*), one does not dwell together with those who have broken the precepts;
and in the Radiant Stage (*prabhākari-bhūmi*), one relinquishes all worldly conventional designations (*prajñapti*).
In the Blazing Ground (*Arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), one attains pure, unshakeable faith in the Buddha;
in the Difficult to Conquer Ground (*Sudurjayā-bhūmi*), one gives rise to immeasurable mundane skillful means and supernormal powers to accomplish worldly affairs;
and in the Manifest Ground (*Abhimukhī-bhūmi*), one contemplates the profound law of dependent origination.
In the Stage of Far-Reaching Travel, one skillfully discerns all phenomena with a vast and expansive mind;
in the Immovable Stage, one is able to initiate great acts of adornment and manifest them;
in the Stage of Wondrous Goodness, one attains profound liberation and penetrates worldly activities, acting in accordance with reality without transgression.
Within the Dharma-Cloud Stage (*dharmameghā bhūmi*), one is able to receive the great rain of the Dharma-light from all Buddhas.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
It is like a great maṇi-jewel that possesses ten qualities by which it can provide all manner of precious objects to sentient beings."

What are these ten? First, emerging from the great ocean; second, being refined by a skilled craftsman; third, becoming increasingly exquisite; fourth, having its impurities removed; fifth, being tempered with fire; sixth, being adorned with various jewels; seventh, being strung with precious threads; eighth, being placed upon a high pillar of lapis lazuli; ninth, radiating light in the four directions; and tenth, raining down various precious objects according to the king’s will.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
The jewel of the bodhicitta generated by Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas also has ten aspects. What are these ten?

1. First, giving with the initial arousal of the mind of enlightenment, thereby departing from stinginess; 2. Second, practicing the precepts and the ascetic dhūta austerities; 3. Third, causing them to become increasingly refined and subtle through various dhyānas, liberations, and samādhis; 4. Fourth, purifying them through the practices of the Path; 5. Fifth, refining them with skillful means and supernormal powers (abhijñā); 6. Sixth, adorning them with the profound Dharma of causes and conditions; 7. Seventh, threading them together with various profound skillful means and wisdom; 8. Eighth, placing them upon the banner of sovereign supernormal power; 9. Ninth, observing the conduct of sentient beings and emitting the light of extensive learning and wisdom; 10. Tenth, being invested by all Buddhas with the office of wisdom—at that time, one is able to perform the Buddha-work for all sentient beings and is included within the category of Sarvajña (omniscience).
"O Sons of the Buddha!
This chapter on the Dharma-door of the Collection of All Wisdom and Meritorious Qualities practiced by these Bodhisattvas cannot be heard by those who have not deeply planted roots of goodness."
He asked, "If one were to hear it, how much merit would that person obtain? He replied:

"Whatever merit is encompassed by the object of focus when one generates the mind of *sarvajñā* (omniscience) in accordance with the wisdom and power of wisdom possessed by all Buddhas, the merit obtained by this person upon hearing this Dharma-gate is likewise the same."

Why is this? If one lacks the bodhicitta, one will be unable to believe, understand, receive, and uphold this Dharma-gate upon hearing it; how much less could one cultivate it with the body and accomplish such a feat?
O Sons of the Buddha!
For this reason, you should know that such a person accords with all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), having heard it, gained faith and understanding, received and upheld it, and practiced it.

While this sutra was being spoken, through the Buddha’s supernatural power, worlds in the ten directions—ten billion buddha-fields, as numerous as the atoms of those worlds—trembled in six ways and eighteen manners.
Furthermore, the earth should tremble;

the various devas should rain down flowers like clouds, raining down incense, necklaces, celestial jewel-robes, celestial banners and canopies, celestial precious objects, and celestial ornaments for the body, while celestial music, songs, and hymns descend as rain.

Furthermore, there was a great sound praising the sublime excellence of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*). Thus, within the four continents of the palace of the King of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven, and likewise throughout all worlds in the ten directions, the *Daśabhūmika Sūtra* was being proclaimed everywhere.

By the spiritual power of the Buddha, there came from the worlds of the ten directions—worlds as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields—bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields, filling the void of the ten directions, all of whom spoke these words:
"Excellent, excellent!
Vajragarbha! Son of the Buddha, you have well explained the characteristics of the stages in which the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas abide.
Son of the Buddha!

We are all likewise named Vajragarbha, having come from the presence of the Buddha Vajradhvaja in the world Vajraguṇa. In every place we have visited, we have preached this sutra; the assemblies were just like this, the words were just like this, and the meaning was just like this—neither more nor less.
"O Sons of the Buddha!
By the power of the Buddha, we have come to this great assembly to bear witness to this matter.
O Sons of the Buddha!"

Just as we have come to this assembly, so too, in every world-system throughout the ten directions, within the maṇi-jewel palaces of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven kings atop each of the four continents, there are bodhisattvas numbering as many as the atoms in ten billion buddha-fields who have gone there to serve as witnesses.

At that time, Vajragarbha Bodhisattva surveyed the ten directions, beheld the entire great assembly, and contemplated the profound nature of phenomena; he praised the arousal of the mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*) and demonstrated to sentient beings the great power of bodhisattvas.

Desiring to purify all bodhisattva practices, to gather in all sentient beings, to accord with omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), to remove all the defilements of the world, and to provide for all sentient beings the causal conditions for the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*), he manifested inconceivable, wondrous adornments of wisdom and expounded the distinct characteristics of all the merits of bodhisattvas.
In order to further clarify this meaning and reveal it to sentient beings, he received the Buddha’s spiritual power and spoke these verses:
“The practices of all bodhisattvas Delight in sublime tranquility;
Their minds are without attachment, Just like empty space.”
Having removed the stains of greed, hatred, and delusion, and dwelling securely within the wisdom of the Path—
such supreme conduct as this, I pray and desire to hear.
Thus these bodhisattvas, throughout immeasurable eons,
have with diligent minds constantly cultivated ten trillion kinds of roots of goodness,
making offerings to immeasurable Buddhas, pratyekabuddhas, and arhats.
For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, he gave rise to the bodhicitta.
Diligently observing the precepts and practicing dhūta austerities, he removed the stains of sin;
cultivating wholesome patience that turns toward the sublime, he was filled with the majesty of shame and remorse.
By virtue of the causes and conditions of merit and wisdom, their lofty and superior minds are luminous and pure;
deeply delighting in the Buddha’s knowledge, they give birth to bodhicitta just as the Buddhas do.
They make offerings to all the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time.
May lands as vast as space be made entirely pure.
Because they have thoroughly mastered the equality of all phenomena,
they give rise to the bodhicitta in order to deliver all sentient beings.
All these bodhisattvas likewise give rise to such immeasurable minds;
reaching the Stage of Joy, they cease evil and delight in giving.
Having attained the power of their original vows, their hearts of compassion and mercy are especially abundant.
Deeply practicing the ten paths of wholesome action, one can reach the Ground Free from Defilement.
Rich in the merit of precepts and learning, with a compassionate heart pitying the world,
forever free from all impurities, the deep mind is ever pure.
Universally observing all worlds, where the fires of the three poisons blaze intensely,
such a Great Being is able to enter the stage of the Three Knowledges.
He contemplates that the three realms are entirely empty, impermanent, and like a disease.
Like an abscess, like a wound pierced by an arrow, a hundred kinds of suffering are ever-present;
seeing the faults of all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) and clinging to the Buddha’s merits,
one attains the blazing radiance of the Buddha’s wisdom and enters the Stage of Blazing Radiance (*Arciṣmatī-bhūmi*).
Having achieved mindfulness and wisdom, they attain the knowledge of the Path;
dwelling in this stage, they make offerings to hundreds of thousands of Buddhas,
and are always able to contemplate and remember the immeasurable virtues of all Buddhas.
Having attained entry into all things, they reach the world’s stage that is difficult to conquer.
Through wisdom and skillful means, they manifest in various ways;
whatever deeds they perform, they do so for the benefit of the world.
Making offerings to all Buddhas and performing deeds that benefit sentient beings,
with the dharma of non-arising before them, they enter the Stage of Presence (*abhimukhī-bhūmi*).
All the practices of the Bodhisattvas are difficult for anyone in the world to know.
Always free from the notion of a self, detached from both existence and non-existence;
all phenomena are primordially empty and quiescent, yet they proceed by way of the twelve links of dependent origination.
One who thoroughly understands this subtle [process] is able to enter the Ground of Far-Going.
Practicing wisdom, skillful means, and so forth, they attain the mark of the quiescence of dharmas;
such great beings are difficult to know and difficult to reach.
Yet, for the sake of causing the world to attain sublime quiescence, they manifest their presence.
Returning to the practice of various deeds and diverse meritorious acts,
they enter universally into the various mental dispositions of sentient beings;
thus they are able to enter the Immovable Ground, which is equal to space.
The Bodhisattvas of great wisdom are all fully capable of practicing various deeds of knowledge; they attain the ten powers of mastery.
With immeasurable and boundless bodies, they...
Universally manifesting throughout the realms of the ten directions, they preach the wondrous Dharma;
thoroughly penetrating the nature of the world and the nature of all sentient beings,
such great compassion enables them to enter the stage of sublime goodness.
With the foremost, wondrously pure wisdom, he skillfully observes all worlds;
for the sake of delivering those who are ensnared by the threads of afflictions and karma in deep,
crooked, and perilous places, he has attained the treasury of all Buddha-dharmas.
He excellently expounds the ultimate truth, entirely without error or contradiction.
Practicing in such a sequence, he fulfills all wholesome dharmas,
reaching even to the ninth stage, having cultivated and accumulated merit and wisdom.
Desiring to attain the powers of all Buddhas, the foremost profound and wondrous benefit,
one is then able to receive the office of wisdom from all Buddhas.
Having first attained countless meditative concentrations, the practice of wisdom becomes exceedingly vast.
At the very end, one attains the indestructible, the office of all wisdoms, and samādhi. If one can attain such as this—
the office of all [wisdoms] and the adornment of all jewels— then the great lotus immediately emerges.
The Bodhisattva named Padma manifested his body sitting upon it;
all the other Bodhisattvas of the various flowers gazed upon him with a single mind.
At that time, the Great Bodhisattva emitted from his body immeasurable [rays].
Hundreds of billions of rays of light extinguish all the sufferings of the world.
Thereafter, from the crown of his head, hundreds of billions of rays of light emerge,
universally illuminating the worlds of the ten directions and the great assemblies of all Buddhas.
In the empty space above, they transform into a net of light;
having made offerings to all Buddhas, it enters beneath the feet of all Buddhas.
At that time, all the Buddhas and all the great Bodhisattvas—
Each [Buddha] knows that this bodhisattva has received the office of wisdom.
All such Buddhas respond with light from between their eyebrows,
called "The Office of All," which enters the crown of this bodhisattva’s head.
All the immeasurable Buddhas confer this bodhisattva office upon him,
just as a wheel-turning monarch provisionally bestows the rank of crown prince.
At that time, all the worlds of the ten directions tremble greatly throughout.
Even down to the Avīci hell and all other realms, all sufferings are extinguished.
For the sake of all beings, the Bodhisattva attains this office through wisdom;
thus it is called reaching the Unsurpassed Stage of the Dharma-Cloud.
Abiding within this stage, their wisdom is boundless;
They skillfully know how to deliver all beings from the various causes and conditions of the world.
They enter into the dharmas of the form and formless realms, as well as the desire, form, and formless worlds.
They are able to know the nature of sentient beings, the nature of lands, and the nature of phenomena;
they can further enter into both countable and uncountable dharmas,
and even proceed to contemplate and discern the immeasurable nature of empty space.
Upon entering this stage, one fully possesses all the miraculous transformations of Bodhisattvas,
the majestic spiritual powers of the Buddhas, and the subtle, secret matters of wisdom. Furthermore,
one is able to thoroughly penetrate the calculations of all kalpas.
Within a single hair-tip, one perceives the nature of the world.
All Tathāgatas, upon this unsurpassed stage, manifest their initial birth,
renunciation of the home, attainment of the Way, and turning of the wheel of Dharma.
They manifest entry into nirvana, all in accordance with wisdom;
this wondrous liberation of tranquil extinction is entirely attained on this stage.
Because the power of mindfulness of the great beings of this stage is so vast, [they act thus].
The great Dharma rain of all Buddhas, they are able to receive and uphold it all.
Just as the waters of the great ocean can sustain the rain of the dragon kings;
so too do Bodhisattvas receive the great Dharma rain of all Buddhas.
If, in the presence of a single Buddha, one hears and receives the Dharma at one time,
then throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions,
sentient beings as numerous as motes of dust shall all hear this dhāraṇī and achieve the Śrāvaka Vehicle.
This is not like that of these bodhisattvas, which is beyond the reach of calculation.
By the power of great wisdom and the arising of the power of great vows,
they are able, within a single thought-moment, to pervade immeasurable lands.
Raining down the nectar-like water of the Dharma, It extinguishes the fires of all afflictions;
Therefore, the Buddhas name this stage The Cloud of Dharma.
When a Great Being dwells on this stage, They provide all manner of offerings to the Buddhas.
Surpassing all that belongs to the devas, he universally displays great supernormal powers.
He manifests to the assembly a power even more supreme, exceeding these numbers by the immeasurable;
if a person should wish to calculate it, they would become bewildered and unable to comprehend it.
When one of great wisdom dwells in this stage, even the act of lifting and lowering the feet cannot be known by other bodhisattvas up to those on the ninth stage, let alone by other sentient beings.
The śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas of the three periods of time—
All these Buddhas dwelling here reveal to them the matters of all-encompassing wisdom,
And cause them to attain thorough penetration; This is the unimpeded knowledge of the three periods of time.
He also demonstrates the quiescence of the nature of phenomena, and he also displays various transformations;
throughout all worlds, for all classes of sentient beings,
he reveals every dharma they practice and all matters that are profound, subtle, hidden, and wondrous.
The merits of all Buddhas are shown in succession so that they may be known.
When a Bodhisattva dwells in this stage, they are able to use great articles of offering to make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions, filling all quarters.
Among all the worlds, none of the various classes of sentient beings nor any other offerings can equal it.
When the wise dwell on this stage, they are able to shatter everything.
The various darknesses of ignorance are illuminated by the Buddha-way;
just as the sovereign King of Devas extinguishes all heat and affliction with his light,
so too does the wisdom-light of the Buddha’s sons extinguish all afflictions.
Abiding in this stage, they all act as sovereign kings over the three realms;
They penetrate all forms of wisdom and skillfully transform beings through the three vehicles.
Within a single thought-moment, they attain immeasurable samādhis.
"One can see the Buddhas of the ten directions, their number being likewise thus.
Bodhisattva Vajragarbha addressed the great beings, saying:
"I have now briefly explained the wondrous practices of the ten stages."
If one were to explain it in detail, it would not be exhausted even in a thousand billion eons;
this is called the Pure Grounds of the Great Bodhisattvas.
For the sake of attaining the Buddha’s wisdom, they dwell within these grounds.
Abiding immovably, like the king of great mountains;
In the first stage, he possesses all scriptures and various arts and crafts,
Like the king of snowy mountains, which accumulates all medicinal herbs.
Maintaining the precepts and possessing great learning, dwelling within these two stages,
is like the King of Fragrant Mountains, which gathers all manner of perfumes;
or like Mount Kailāsa, where many precious flowers are heaped together.
On the Ground of Radiance, one gathers the wisdom of hearing; its analogy is likewise so.
On the Ground of Blazing, there is much accumulation; the jewels of the Dharma-path are indestructible.
Like within the mountains of seers and sages, those who are well-peaceful are not few.
The various supernormal powers of the fifth stage cannot be equaled by any;
they are like Mount Yugaṃdhara, where the yakṣa deities are numerous.
On the sixth stage, one skillfully discriminates, and the various fruits are inexhaustible.
Just as Mount Aśvakarṇa has immeasurable fruits,
so too among those of great wisdom on the seventh stage, none can equal them;
just as Mount Nimindhara has no small number of nāga kings.
Abiding in the eighth stage, their sovereign wisdom is immeasurable;
like Mount Cakravāḍa, they are masters of many minds.
In the ninth stage, their minds are pure, and they preach the Dharma without obstruction.
Just as Mount Cakravāḍa is not lacking in asuras,
so too the Buddhas within the ten stages possess inexhaustible merit;
like Sumeru, the king of mountains, they are surrounded by a vast multitude of celestial deities.
Furthermore, in the first stage, one gives rise to vast vows;
in the second stage, one maintains the category of ethical discipline; in the third stage, one practices meritorious deeds;
in the fourth stage, one is single-mindedly focused; and in the fifth stage, there are manifold wondrous matters.
The sixth stage is the mark of profundity; the seventh stage is the vast mind;
the eighth stage consists of various kinds of adornments and supernormal powers;
the ninth stage is the contemplation of wondrous wisdom, which is able to transcend all worlds.
The ten stages can receive and uphold the great rain of the Dharma of all Buddhas.
The ocean of the Bodhisattva’s practice is difficult to move and inexhaustible;
having resolved to transcend the world, one attains entry into the first stage.
In the second stage, one purely maintains the precepts; in the third, one cultivates various dhyānas;
in the fourth, the path-practice is purified; in the fifth, one refines skillful means and wisdom;
in the sixth, one is adorned by causes and conditions; in the seventh, skillful means and wisdom are profound.
The eighth is reaching the Vaidūrya Banner; the ninth stage is for those beings who practice, universally illuminating all places of peril and difficulty with the light of wisdom;
the tenth stage receives the office of knowledge, just as a king grants his permission.
In this manner, through successive purifications, the wondrous jewel of the bodhicitta—
though its number of atoms filling all worlds throughout the ten directions may be calculated and known within a single thought-moment; [the merit of the bodhicitta remains beyond measure].
"One might, with a single hair-tip, count all things within the void;
yet the great merits of the Buddhas are immeasurable and inexhaustible.

When this *Daśabhūmika Sūtra* was being spoken, the Sovereign King of Heaven and his celestial hosts, the Bodhisattva Vimukticandra and the other bodhisattvas, and all the world, were filled with great joy, and they received, believed, and practiced it accordingly.
